text:
Alex P: Heads-up — planning a focused perf run for the embed/rerank endpoint. Goal: isolate kernel-selection + batching heuristics + KV-cache behavior. Comparing two harnesses: synthetic poisson-style generator vs replay_harness using prod traces.

Maria G: Nice. Which model and vector dims are we testing? payload sizes?

Alex P: Targeting the 1024-dim embed model (open-embed-1024-q4) and the 768 baseline for apples-to-apples. Payloads: single-doc ~800B, batch payloads sum up to ~300KB. We'll sweep batch sizes and concurrency.

Ben H: I ran a quick 15m smoke. Synthetic harness (poisson qps target) vs replay_harness (trace from 2026-02-21). Results (1024-dim, batching=auto):
```
synthetic: qps=250, throughput_tokens/s=480k, p50=22ms, p95=180ms, p99=420ms, kv_cache_hit=12%
replay:    qps=250, throughput_tokens/s=455k, p50=26ms, p95=210ms, p99=620ms, kv_cache_hit=8%
```
Notice replay has worse tail and lower cache hits (more random prefixes).

Kevin L: That's concerning — I saw a tail regression after kernel-selector v2 landed. On high-concurrency runs the selector falls back to fp32 GEMM for some dims/seq combos. nvprof snapshot: `sgemm_int8_opt: 3.2ms` vs `sgemm_fp32_fallback: 11.9ms` for the same op when sequence-length > 2048 (edge case for rerank).

Alex P: Do we have the exact commit that introduced the selector change? We need an apples-to-apples: same model commit, same compile flags, only swap kernel selector.

Ben H: Commit: a1b2c3d4 (kernel-selection: heuristics v2). I re-ran with selector pinned to v1 on the same build: p99 dropped from 620ms to 250ms under replay harness. So the selector heuristics are choosing a slower kernel for certain batched shapes.

Maria G: Can you paste the command you used for the replay run?

Ben H: Sure: 
```
./tools/replay_harness \
  --trace=s3://replays/rerank-prod-2026-02-21.json \
  --qps=250 \
  --concurrency=80 \
  --batching=auto \
  --pin-kernel-selector=a1b2c3d4-v1 \
  --stats=/tmp/bench_replay.json
```

Alex P: Good. Two hypotheses: (1) selector logic weights FP32 stability higher for long sequences leading to fallback; (2) batching heuristic creates heterogeneous batches and causes stragglers that force timeouts and kernel fallback due to memory alignment.

Kevin L: Profiler traces show memcpy spikes on CPU->GPU around the same window as the tail spikes. Looks like dynamic reformatting to FP32 before kernel launch. Flamegraph snippet from nsight: `host memcpy` -> `reformat_to_fp32` -> `sgemm_fp32_fallback`.

Maria G: Could KV cache behavior be influencing this? If cache hits are low (replay case) we end up with longer prefixes per request and more variable sequence lengths. That could push shapes into a different codepath.

Alex P: Exactly — replay shows more variance in seq length distribution. For apples-to-apples we should normalize by truncating/padding sequences so both harnesses present the same length histogram. Also capture kv_cache_hit rate and report by-percentile of seq lengths.

Ben H: Agreed. I also experimented with a batching tweak: cap max-batch-bytes to 256KB and use length-percentile cutoff (p95) to form batches. With that, replay p99 improved ~25% and p95 ~10%. Config snippet: 
```
batching:
  max_batch_bytes: 262144
  length_grouping: p95
  eviction_policy: oldest_first
```

Kevin L: Proposal: run 3 controlled experiments (all with same build/commit):
1) synthetic harness with original batching & selector v2
2) replay harness with original batching & selector v2\3) replay harness with length-normalized inputs + selector v2 + capped batches
Collect per-op kernel selection logs, nvprof traces, kv cache hit rates, batch composition histogram, and p50/p95/p99.

Alex P: Sounds good. Add these constraints: fixed random seed for synthetic generator, 30-minute runs each, and collect traces at 1s resolution. Also ensure we tag runs with commit + build id (build-2026.03.01-a1b2c3).

Ben H: I'll start experiment 1 now, kicking off at 1772012400. Will upload stats to `/artifacts/embed-rerank/1772012345/`.

Loadbot: run-started: replay_harness run_id=run-1772012345-1 (metadata attached)

Maria G: If we see selector v2 choosing worse kernels systematically, we should fallback to v1 for rerank workloads until heuristics are improved. Also we need an automated unit test for kernel_selector that feeds varied batch shapes.

Kevin L: I'll open a PR with a deterministic selector test and a small fix to avoid promoting FP32 for quantized-friendly shapes. ETA EOD.

Alex P: Next steps summary: (1) Ben to finish runs and upload artifacts; (2) Kevin to add deterministic selector test + small heuristic guard; (3) Maria to prepare normalized trace for apples-to-apples; (4) Alex will collate results and create a short postmortem if we confirm regression. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Ben H: ack, starting now. :rocket:
